clue.text: Musicians showed emotion, affected by moving air

parts.note: the winds are the wind-instrument players of an orchestra
wept means cried, showing feeling

explanation.surface: Players in a band grew tearful while a breeze blew over them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musicians' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is the woodwind and brass section, the WINDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A place exposed to strong gusts is described as swept by them, so the adjective suits anything buffeted by gales.

clue.text: Champagne for Mrs. Bardell, for example

definitions.meaning: the ... is slang for champagne, from the Veuve Clicquot brand, veuve meaning ... in French
Mrs Bardell is the ... landlady who sues Mr Pickwick in Dickens's Pickwick Papers

explanation.definitionFit: Veuve, the French word on a famous champagne label, means a woman whose husband has died, as Dickens's landlady was.

clue.text: Woman's garment seen near man's

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near
a tie is a garment typically worn by a man

explanation.surface: A lady's clothing is displayed next to a gentleman's.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose dress worn to bed is women's nightwear.

clue.text: Get leg broken in London street, or suffocated

indicators.note: in puts the reordered letters inside the street name

parts.note: the Strand is a famous street in central London

indicators.note: broken tells us the letters of the limb word are smashed and reordered

explanation.surface: A pedestrian breaks a leg on a London road or is choked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is a link word; the Strand is a famous London street, and 'broken' and 'in' are the operations, despite the surface's injured pedestrian.
explanation.definitionFit: Choked to death by having the throat squeezed means deprived of air.

clue.text: Redundant tramp runs away over the top

parts.note: extra means surplus, more than needed

indicators.note: away signals the abbreviation being taken out of the word for the wanderer

parts.note: a vagrant is a homeless wanderer
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A surplus vagabond dashes off excessively.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish beyond reason, going too far, is what the idiom over the top means.

clue.text: Save up for boat

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: save means except, as does but

explanation.surface: Putting money by in order to buy a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a verb about money; it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is slang for a slow, clumsy vessel.

clue.text: Performing a sort of dance, and available

parts.note: on means appearing on stage, performing
tap is a style of dance done in metal-tipped shoes

explanation.surface: A dancer is on stage doing a routine and ready for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer drawn from a cask is ready to serve, so the idiom means ready for use whenever wanted.

clue.text: Bulb lit before and after one

parts.note: a light that is lit is switched on
I is the Roman numeral one
a light that is lit is switched on

explanation.surface: A light bulb was switched on before and after a single moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before and after one' says the word for lit goes on both sides of the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable grows as a layered underground bulb.

clue.text: Material producing turnover for big cheese

indicators.note: turnover says the word for big is flipped so its letters run backwards

parts.note: fat means large or big
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A fabric that gives a company income for a top boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big cheese' looks like one phrase for a boss; split it into big and cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, glossy fabric, so it is a cloth or material.

clue.text: Columns about court by one old writer

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
I is the Roman numeral one
a style was an old pointed writing implement, a stylus

explanation.surface: Articles about a tennis court by a long-dead author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Columns' suggests newspaper writing and 'old writer' an author; both are literal, pillars and a stylus.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical architecture a ring of pillars surrounding a courtyard is exactly that structure.

clue.text: Pursue left-winger in moderate movement

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
a Trot is a Trotskyist, a far-left activist

explanation.surface: Hounding a socialist activist at a steady pace.
explanation.walkthrough: TROT is informal for a Trotskyist, a common crossword 'left-winger'.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy jog at a gentle pace, like a dog trotting, is a steady, unhurried gait.

clue.text: Cut more cheese for each roll, initially

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A shopper asks for extra slices of cheese for every bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut more' looks like an instruction to slice; read it as an adjective, more cut down or shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shorter than another is more curtailed, the comparative of short and concise.

clue.text: German warhead destroyed a town

indicators.note: destroyed tells us the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A German missile laid waste to a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German warhead' reads as a missile, but it is the head of the German gods, a war god.
explanation.definitionFit: In Germanic myth the chief god, counterpart of the Norse Odin, ruled the gods and presided over battle.

clue.text: Sailors with quarters beside river they're missing

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; ABS is plural
east and north are two of the compass quarters, E and N
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Seamen with lodgings by a river are absent from duty.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points E, N, S and W are the crossword's 'quarters'.
explanation.definitionFit: People who fail to turn up are not present, which is what the plural noun names.

clue.text: National hero dismantled segregation

indicators.note: dismantled says the word is taken apart and its letters put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A patriotic figure broke down racial separation.
explanation.definitionFit: The dragon-slaying saint is England's patron, a figure of national legend.

clue.text: Protected area, in general

definitions.meaning: the sheltered side away from the wind
Robert E. ..., the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means shelter from the wind, and it is also the surname of the famous Confederate commander.

clue.text: Member's no longer with us to do parliamentary business

parts.note: a leg is a member or limb, and the 's stands for is
late means dead

explanation.surface: An MP has died, leaving others to carry on with legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a Member of Parliament, fitting the surface; it is a limb, LEG, with 's read as IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Making laws is the core work of a parliament, so the verb means doing that business.

clue.text: Usheress an important person in theatre?

definitions.text: Usheress an important person in theatre?

parts.words: Usheress an important person in theatre?
parts.note: a woman who shows patrons to their seats guides them along, so she is a woman doing the guiding; in theatre the same phrase means the star actress

explanation.surface: Asking whether the woman who shows you to your seat matters in a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal female role in a play or film is taken by the star actress, and an usheress literally guides people.

clue.text: Plant European's embarrassed to turn up in

parts.note: a German is a European; the 's is a link meaning is

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reverses the word so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: red means flushed with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A continental visitor is ashamed to arrive at a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a herb of the mint family, so it is a plant.

clue.text: A lot of money needed to defeat tough opponent on board

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars
to master is to overcome or defeat

explanation.surface: A large sum is required to beat a strong chess rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess player of the highest title is a formidable adversary across the chessboard.

clue.text: Greed shown by Virginia, tucking into a sort of pudding

indicators.note: tucking into places the state's abbreviation inside the other letters

parts.note: rice pudding is a kind of dessert
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia greedily eats a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sounds like Virginia eating the pudding, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive desire for wealth is a synonym for greed.

clue.text: Sporting equipment one player may get from another

definitions.meaning: the long stick used in snooker or billiards

definitions.text: one player may get from another
definitions.meaning: in theatre, an actor's prompt to speak comes from another actor's line

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a snooker stick and the signal line an actor waits for before speaking.

clue.text: He doesn't act originally to "imitate the action of the tiger"

definitions.text: imitate the action of the tiger
definitions.meaning: to copy a cat, quoting Henry V's battle speech

explanation.definitionFit: A mimic who copies others is called by this name, and taken literally it is to copy a cat such as a tiger.

clue.text: Act to enter SF movie for Oscar, say

indicators.note: to enter signals one piece going inside another, here the film title inside the law

parts.note: an Act of Parliament is a statute
E.T. is Spielberg's science-fiction film

explanation.surface: Performing in a science-fiction film to win an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' here has the film going into the Act, though the surface implies the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is a small gold figurine, and a small sculpted figure is exactly that kind of trophy.

clue.text: Make one article abroad if it takes a year

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Unite a foreign piece of writing if it lasts twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite separate parts into a single whole is to join them together.

clue.text: A Northerner, taken aback, is in shock

indicators.note: taken aback says the word for the northerner is read backwards

parts.note: a Lapp is a native of Lapland in the far north of Europe

explanation.surface: Someone from the far north is startled and stunned.
explanation.definitionFit: To horrify or dismay someone is to shock them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Colour used in vessel I lacquered

indicators.note: used in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A shade of paint used on a vase that has been lacquered.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple shade, named after the flowering shrub.

clue.text: Book I set in parts of Italy given as gift

indicators.note: set in places one group of letters inside another
parts of suggests the country's name is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A novel of mine is set in various regions of Italy and handed over as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' breaks ITALY into ALITY; 'set in' puts B and I after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural talent or aptitude is often called a gift, as in having a gift for music.

clue.text: Conclusions reached by jury are consistent so far

indicators.note: Conclusions points to the final letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: The jury's verdicts have been in agreement up to now.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, until now, is a sense of the adverb, as in not finished yet.

clue.text: Conservative, in diverging from centre, becomes extreme

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for spreading outwards

parts.note: radial lines spread outwards from a central point

explanation.surface: A Tory drifting from the political middle turns into a firebrand.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about politics; 'diverging from centre' is a geometric description of spokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A view far from the mainstream and favouring sweeping change is drastic, at the political edge.

clue.text: Time for opposition?

definitions.meaning: time is called the old foe in the saying about time being against us
the opposing side in a war or contest

explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially time is the foe of us all, and the word also names the opposing side in a conflict.

clue.text: Getting the soldiers to call back may be impractical

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: back says the word for summon runs right to left

parts.note: to cite is to summon, as a witness is called

explanation.surface: Bringing the troops in to be recalled might not be workable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas worked out in the abstract rather than tested in use are unworkable, existing only on paper.
